proposed_relationship: Encapsulating modified-nucleoside mRNA that encodes for the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in lipid nanoparticles can efficiently deliver the mRNA into cells, triggering an immune response without being degraded by TLR7/8.
mechanism: The mechanism involves the use of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to deliver the modified-nucleoside mRNA into the cytoplasm of cells, where it can be translated into the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, triggering an immune response and the production of neutralizing antibodies. The modification of the mRNA with pseudouridine or N1-methylpseudouridine reduces the recognition by TLR7/8, preventing the degradation of the mRNA and allowing for efficient translation. The resulting spike protein is then recognized by the immune system, leading to the production of neutralizing antibodies.
constraint_released: This approach releases the constraint of requiring months to years of manufacturing scale-up for conventional vaccine platforms.
predicted_quantitative_outcome: A 90% reduction in time-to-market for vaccine development, from years to weeks
